title: Find Proteins of Unknown Function (PUFs) using Plantannot - Protocol C
author: Marcos Viana
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgdijs4e

steps.title: Open Plantannot search page
steps.instruction: Navigate to https://www.machado.cnptia.embrapa.br/plantannot or directly to https://www.machado.cnptia.embrapa.br/plantannot/find/?q= with all filters and the search box empty.

steps.title: Select organism filter
steps.instruction: In the Filters panel, expand the “Organisms” filter (green arrow) and select the desired organism, e.g., Oropetium thomaeum, or leave all boxes unchecked to include all organisms. Click “Apply” to apply the filter.

steps.title: Set feature type to polypeptide
steps.instruction: In the Filters panel, choose “polypeptide” under the “Feature type” filter and click “Apply”.

steps.title: Apply analyses filters
steps.instruction: In the “Analyses” filter, check both “diamond matches” (to retrieve proteins already present in the NCBI nr database) and “no interproscan matches” (to exclude proteins with known domains), then click “Apply”.

steps.title: Leave orthology filters empty
steps.instruction: Ensure the “Orthology”, “Coexpression”, and “Orthologs_coexpression” filters remain unchecked (empty).

steps.title: Search for unknown function
steps.instruction: In the main search box, type the phrase “Unknown function” and press the magnifying‑glass icon (or Enter) to run the text search.

steps.title: View filtered results
steps.instruction: The Results card on the centre‑right of the screen will display the list of proteins of unknown function that meet all filters; for Oropetium thomaeum this yields 7 PUFs.
